concepts.title: Root, Stem and Leaf with Their Modifications
concepts.section: 5.2 The Root, 5.3 The Stem, 5.4 The Leaf
concepts.definition: The flowering plant body shows a root system bearing root hairs and root caps, a stem with nodes and internodes bearing buds, and leaves with lamina; each organ shows modifications such as tap and fibrous roots, tubers, tendrils and thorns, and storage or climbing leaves.
concepts.key_idea: Modifications like storage roots of carrot, stem tendrils of cucumber and leaf tendrils of peas reflect adaptation to storage, support and defence functions.

concepts.title: Inflorescence, Flower and Its Parts
concepts.definition: The flower is a modified shoot bearing four whorls of calyx, corolla, androecium and gynoecium arranged on thalamus, and flowers are arranged in racemose or cymose inflorescence; symmetry, merosity, aestivation and placentation describe its structure.
concepts.key_idea: A flower is actinomorphic or zygomorphic, trimerous tetramerous or pentamerous, and its gynoecium may be apocarpous or syncarpous with superior or inferior ovary.

solution_steps.explain: Identify calyx, corolla, androecium and gynoecium in the flower.

concepts.title: Fruit, Seed Structure and Semi-technical Description
concepts.section: 5.7 The Fruit, 5.8 The Seed, 5.9 Description of Plant Families
concepts.definition: After fertilisation the ovary becomes the fruit and ovules become seeds; the seed shows embryo with cotyledons, seed coat and endosperm as in maize, and plants are described in semi-technical language with floral formula and floral diagram, as seen in fabaceae, solanaceae and liliaceae.
concepts.key_idea: The floral formula with its symbols of bract, symmetry, merosity, fusion and ovary position condenses the family characters of fabaceae, solanaceae and liliaceae.

solution_steps.explain: Follow ovary to fruit and ovule to seed after fertilisation.
